text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Europeans weighing Palestinian President Arafat's request to impose economic sanctions on Israel.
- Ben-Gurion airport, railways and government companies on strike today.
GLOBES
- Claridge president Kolber says Claridge intends to have 33 percent stake in Koor.
MAARIV
- Position paper prepared in prime minister's office proposes "independent Palestinian entity whose centre is in the Jerusalem district".
- Wave of strikes, including Tel Aviv airport and El Al.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel prepared to slow building in Jewish settlements.
- Claridge won't be able to merge Tadiran with ECI following purchase of controlling interest in Koor.
- Finance Minister Neeman does not rule out tax hike in 1998.
- Koor to freeze contacts on selling its companies until Claridge deal complete.
- Claridge does not intend to dismiss CEO Benjamin Gaon.
JERUSALEM POST
- Knesset passes early reading of bill to shore up Golan law.
- State workers declare strike.
- Claridge president Kolber: We won't break up Koor.
- World Bank earmarks $10 million for Gaza industrial park.
